keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row for it). The republic claims 266,000 km2 and controls 90,000 km2 ('Total 266,000 km2 (claimed)', '90,000 km2 (controlled)'): the claim is drawn as the shape and the Moroccan and Mauritanian holds are hatched by occupation events. The gazetteer resolves Western Sahara (country W. Sahara, 331 cells) to about 84,000 km2 (ratio 0.93 against the controlled 90,000) and, with the two Moroccan-run regions Laayoune-Boujdour-Sakia el-Hamra and Oued ed-Dahab, to about 220,000 km2 (ratio 0.83 against the claim). The pages disagree on how much the republic holds: one-fifth (SADR and war pages), about 30% (conflict page), 90,000 of 266,000 km2 (infobox, 34%).

ledger.note: 1976: Morocco takes the north. After the Spanish withdrawal of 26 February 1976 'Morocco took over the Saguia El Hamra and the northern two-thirds of the territory' (the page gives no month for the partition).

ledger.note: 1976: Mauritania takes the south of Western Sahara. 'Morocco and Mauritania responded by annexing the territory of Western Sahara' (SADR page); the page gives Mauritania no share, so the south (Tiris al-Gharbiya) is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Free Zone (the 'Liberated Territories'), the part of Western Sahara east of the Moroccan-built Berm

ledger.note: 1976 (27 February): the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic is proclaimed at Bir Lehlou. Infobox 'Republic declared: 27 February 1976'; the proclamation was made in 'the government-in-exile's provisional capital, Bir Lehlou'; Spain had 'informed the UN on 26 February 1976' that it had ended its presence. The core is the desert east of the Moroccan and Mauritanian columns.

ledger.note: 1991 (6 September): the ceasefire. A ceasefire 'came into effect on 6 September 1991'; 'Morocco controls approximately 80% of the territory, the Polisario Front controls 20%' behind and beyond the Berm, which Morocco built from the mid-1980s. The occupation continues.
2008 (27 February): the provisional capital moves from Bir Lehlou to Tifariti ('formally moved to Tifariti' on 27 February 2008).

ledger.note: 2020 (14 November): the ceasefire ends. After the Moroccan army 'entered into the demilitarized town of Guerguerat' on 13 November 2020, Brahim Ghali 'announced that he had signed a decree bringing the 29 year old ceasefire to an end'; the page says the Polisario then controlled about 30% of the territory.

wars.outcome: Stalemate: Mauritania made peace on 5 August 1979 and Morocco annexed its share on 11 August 1979; Morocco built a berm from the mid-1980s and controls about 80%, the Polisario about 20%, after the ceasefire of 6 September 1991.
wars.note: The page's infobox runs '31 October 1975 - 6 September 1991'; the first Moroccan troops reached El Aaiun on 11 December 1975. The Madrid Accords were signed on 14 November 1975 and Spain announced its full withdrawal on 26 February 1976.

wars.name: Western Sahara conflict (2020 renewal)

zones.text: the Free Zone (the 'Liberated Territories'), the part of Western Sahara east of the Moroccan-built Berm

wars.outcome: Fighting resumed after the Guerguerat incident of 13 November 2020 ended the 29-year ceasefire; the pages opened give no change of control and no events for 2023-2024.
wars.note: The conflict page is inconsistent on the date of the US recognition of Moroccan sovereignty (4 or 10 December 2020); UN Security Council text of October 2025 'referenced Morocco's Autonomy Proposal'.

certainty.note: No agreed boundary: the Berm is a military line, the 1991 ceasefire line is the Berm, and Morocco and the Polisario each claim the whole territory. The frontiers with Morocco proper, Algeria and Mauritania are colonial lines not on any page opened.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row for Spanish Sahara or the SADR. The shape here is the republic's claim; what it controls is the Free Zone (gazetteer country 'W. Sahara', about 84,000 km2 against the infobox's 90,000), and the occupation events hatch the rest. The found event's region is the Free Zone, the core; the keyframe is the whole claim.
Not settled: the Spanish Sahara before 1975 (no dossier: Spain's colonial period belongs to the Spanish Empire dossier); the Mauritanian share of 1976 (page silent: the south is the researcher's reading); the date of the Moroccan-Mauritanian partition (Rabat convention of April 1976 is not on the pages); construction dates of the berms (mid-1980s on the war page); the per-cent controlled (20%, 30%, 34% across pages); recognition (36 UN members and South Ossetia per the infobox, 85 'at one time or another'). The Morocco occupation of 1976 and 1979 is still running at 2024, so those occupation_start events have no end; the 2020 contest likewise.
Counterparts: morocco (Cliopatria row; the Moroccan dossier should record the occupation as the mirror), mauritania, kingdom-of-spain (starts 1516 in Cliopatria; Spain's presence ended 26 February 1976). The gazetteer's W. Sahara polygon matches the controlled zone, not the claim; the Moroccan-run regions carry the rest.
